cases.title: Default versus factory
cases.quote: You can also use `default_factory` (but not both at the same time) to define a callable that will be called to generate a default value.
cases.question: In Pydantic 2.10.6, can the same field specify both default and default_factory?
cases.answer: No. Use either a default value or a default_factory, not both.
cases.rubric: Require mutual exclusivity for the same field; do not claim factories are unsupported.

cases.title: Factory dependency order
cases.quote: The default factory can also take a single required argument, in which the case the already validated data will be passed as a dictionary.
cases.question: In Pydantic 2.10.6, what is supplied to a default_factory with one required argument, and may it depend on fields declared later?
cases.answer: It receives a dictionary of already validated data. Only earlier validated fields are available; depending on a later field can fail.
cases.rubric: Require the validated-data dictionary and declaration-order limitation; reject claims all fields or raw inputs are supplied.

cases.title: Validate defaults explicitly
cases.quote: By default, Pydantic will *not* validate default values. The `validate_default` field parameter
cases.question: In Pydantic 2.10.6, are field defaults validated by default, and how can validation of defaults be enabled?
cases.answer: No. Enable validate_default on the field or in model configuration.
cases.rubric: Require disabled-by-default plus validate_default; do not confuse a supplied input value with a default.

cases.title: Unhashable mutable defaults
cases.quote: Pydantic will create a deep copy of the default value when creating each instance of the model:
cases.question: In Pydantic 2.10.6, if a model field has the unhashable default [{}], is that same nested object necessarily shared by every new model instance?
cases.answer: No. Pydantic deep-copies an unhashable default when creating each model instance.
cases.rubric: Require per-instance deep copying in this unhashable-default case; do not generalize to all arbitrary hashable mutable objects.

cases.title: Annotated metadata and static constructors
cases.quote:
The annotated pattern is *not* understood by them, so you should use the normal
assignment form instead.
cases.question: In Pydantic 2.10.6, for static type checkers to synthesize __init__ using default, default_factory, or alias, should these Field arguments be placed only inside Annotated?
cases.answer: No. Use the normal assignment form for these arguments; static type checkers do not understand the annotated pattern for that synthesis.
cases.rubric: Limit the claim to static constructor synthesis; do not claim Pydantic ignores Annotated metadata at runtime.

cases.title: Input-only versus output aliases
cases.quote:
The `alias` parameter is used for both validation _and_ serialization. If you want to use
_different_ aliases for validation and serialization respectively, you can use the`validation_alias`
and `serialization_alias` parameters, which will apply only in their respective use cases.
cases.question: In Pydantic 2.10.6, does Field(validation_alias='username') by itself rename that field in serialized output as well?
cases.answer: No. validation_alias applies to validation only; serialization_alias is the separate output-specific setting.
cases.rubric: Require input/output distinction; by_alias=True does not convert a validation-only alias into a serialization alias.

cases.title: Nested alias paths
cases.quote: In the `'first_name'` field, we are using the alias `'names'` and the index `0` to specify the path to the first name.
cases.question: In Pydantic 2.10.6, what input does Field(validation_alias=AliasPath('names', 0)) read when validating {'names': ['John', 'Doe']}?
cases.answer: It reads the item at index 0 under names, namely 'John', as the field value.
cases.rubric: Require nested key plus list-index traversal; reject treating the whole names list or its second item as the value.

cases.title: Alternative accepted input keys
cases.quote: `AliasChoices` is used to specify a choice of aliases.
cases.question: In Pydantic 2.10.6, how can a field accept either input key 'first_name' or 'fname' without defining two separate model fields?
cases.answer: Use validation_alias=AliasChoices('first_name', 'fname').
cases.rubric: Require AliasChoices or an equivalent explicit validation_alias construction; do not claim both keys are simultaneously required.

cases.title: Different loading and saving conventions
cases.quote: You can use an `AliasGenerator` to specify different alias generators for validation and serialization.
cases.question: In Pydantic 2.10.6, can a model generate uppercase input aliases and title-case output aliases without assigning each field's aliases individually?
cases.answer: Yes. Configure an AliasGenerator with separate validation_alias and serialization_alias callables.
cases.rubric: Require separate generator functions for the two directions; one ordinary callable does not independently express both conventions.

cases.title: Override an explicit field alias
cases.quote: * `alias_priority=1` the alias *will* be overridden by the alias generator.
cases.question: In Pydantic 2.10.6, with an alias_generator and an explicit Field(alias='lang'), what does alias_priority=1 change compared with the default explicit-alias precedence?
cases.answer: By default the explicit alias wins; alias_priority=1 permits the generated alias to override it.
cases.rubric: Require the direction of precedence and the priority-1 exception; do not swap priority 1 and 2.

cases.title: Strict integer inputs
cases.quote:
For example, when validating an `int` field, only instances of `int` are accepted; passing instances of `float` or `str`
will result in raising a `ValidationError`.
cases.question: In Pydantic 2.10.6, when validating Python data in strict mode for an int field, are the float 1.0 and string '1' accepted through coercion?
cases.answer: No. Those float and string inputs raise validation errors rather than being coerced to int.
cases.rubric: Limit the answer to strict Python validation of an int field; do not claim lax mode has the same behavior or infer unrelated subclass edge cases.

cases.title: Strict JSON differs from Python
cases.quote: instances of `str` will be accepted when validating from JSON, but not from python:
cases.question: In Pydantic 2.10.6, under strict validation of a UUID field, is a UUID string accepted identically from a Python dictionary and from JSON?
cases.answer: No. A UUID string can be accepted from JSON in strict mode, while the same string in Python data is rejected.
cases.rubric: Require the Python-versus-JSON distinction; reject a blanket claim that strict mode rejects all string representations in JSON.

cases.title: Strictness on one field
cases.quote: Only the fields for which `strict=True` is set will be affected:
cases.question: In Pydantic 2.10.6, if only age is declared Field(strict=True), does that automatically make an otherwise ordinary n_pets: int field strict when constructing the model?
cases.answer: No. The field-level strict setting affects age; other ordinary fields retain their own normal validation behavior.
cases.rubric: Require field-level isolation; do not confuse this with a separate model-wide or per-call strict setting.

cases.title: Incomplete JSON prefix
cases.quote:
result = from_json(partial_json_data, allow_partial=True)
print(result)  # (3)!
#> ['aa', 'bb']
cases.question: In Pydantic 2.10.6, using pydantic_core.from_json on the incomplete input '["aa", "bb", "c', what can allow_partial=True recover?
cases.answer: The complete prefix ['aa', 'bb']; the incomplete final string is not recovered as a complete item.
cases.rubric: Require the two complete items and omission of the unfinished item; do not claim the entire malformed input becomes valid or include 'c' as a completed string.

cases.title: Model defaults for incomplete inputs
cases.quote: For partial JSON parsing to work reliably, all fields on the model should have default values.
cases.question: In Pydantic 2.10.6, what field-default design does the documentation recommend when validating models from partially parsed JSON?
cases.answer: Give all model fields default values so missing portions can be handled reliably.
cases.rubric: Describe a reliability recommendation, not a claim that every partial payload without defaults always fails or that requiredness disappears automatically.

cases.title: Cache keys without all values
cases.quote: * `'keys'`: cache only dictionary keys, this **only** applies when used with [`pydantic_core.from_json`][pydantic_core.from_json] or when parsing JSON using [`Json`][pydantic.types.Json]
cases.question: In Pydantic 2.10.6, what does cache_strings='keys' cache, and is that mode documented as applying indiscriminately to every validation path?
cases.answer: It caches dictionary keys only, with the documented scope of pydantic_core.from_json or JSON parsing through Json.
cases.rubric: Require key-only caching and the stated scope; do not confuse this parser cache with an application answer cache or promise lower memory in every workload.

cases.title: Accepted schema extras
cases.quote: You can pass a `dict` or a `Callable` to `json_schema_extra`.
cases.question: In Pydantic 2.10.6, is json_schema_extra restricted to a static dictionary, or can it also accept a callable?
cases.answer: It can accept either a dictionary or a callable.
cases.rubric: Require both accepted forms; do not claim arbitrary mixed dict/callable composition is supported.

cases.title: Combine annotated schema dictionaries
cases.quote: Starting in v2.9, Pydantic merges `json_schema_extra` dictionaries from annotated types.
cases.question: In Pydantic 2.10.6, when a reused Annotated type and a further annotation provide json_schema_extra dictionaries with different keys, does the later dictionary necessarily replace the earlier dictionary entirely?
cases.answer: No. The documented v2.9+ behavior merges the dictionaries additively, preserving their different keys.
cases.rubric: Require additive dictionary merging for the stated distinct-key case; do not invent same-key conflict rules or support for composing dictionaries with callables.

cases.title: Override a field's base JSON schema
cases.quote:
Note that this overrides the whole JSON Schema generation process
for the field (in the following example, the `'type'` also needs to be provided).
cases.question: In Pydantic 2.10.6, does WithJsonSchema merely append a few keys to a field's automatically generated base schema, so the type key can always be omitted?
cases.answer: No. It overrides the field's generated base schema; provide the required schema details, including type in the documented example.
cases.rubric: Require replacement rather than automatic merging of an omitted base type; do not claim this changes runtime value validation.

cases.title: Generated schema specification
cases.start: Pydantic allows automatic creation and customization of JSON schemas from models.
cases.quote: * [JSON Schema Draft 2020-12](https://json-schema.org/draft/2020-12/release-notes.html)
cases.question: In Pydantic 2.10.6, which JSON Schema draft do the generated schemas document compliance with?
cases.answer: JSON Schema Draft 2020-12.
cases.rubric: Require 2020-12 rather than a different draft; do not infer that every unrelated OpenAPI document or externally customized schema uses it.

cases.title: References versus definition storage
cases.end: ## Miscellaneous Notes on JSON Schema Generation
cases.quote: The definitions are always stored under the key `$defs`, but a specified prefix can be used for the references.
cases.question: In Pydantic 2.10.6, if ref_template changes references to '#/components/schemas/{model}', does that by itself move generated definitions out of $defs?
cases.answer: No. ref_template changes the reference format; definitions remain stored under $defs.
cases.rubric: Require separating reference formatting from definition placement; do not claim the option automatically restructures an OpenAPI components object.

cases.title: Sorting exception for properties
cases.quote:
By default, Pydantic recursively sorts JSON schemas by alphabetically sorting keys. Notably, Pydantic skips sorting the values of the `properties` key,
to preserve the order of the fields as they were defined in the model.
cases.question: In Pydantic 2.10.6, does the default recursive JSON-schema key sorting also alphabetize a model's properties instead of preserving field declaration order?
cases.answer: No. Properties are the documented exception: their field order is preserved.
cases.rubric: Require the properties exception while retaining the general sorting rule; do not claim all schema keys retain insertion order.

cases.title: Omit schema without removing validation
cases.quote:
The [`SkipJsonSchema`][pydantic.json_schema.SkipJsonSchema] annotation can be used to skip a including field (or part of a field's specifications)
from the generated JSON schema.
cases.question: In Pydantic 2.10.6, which annotation is documented for omitting a field or part of its specification from generated JSON schema?
cases.answer: SkipJsonSchema.
cases.rubric: Identify SkipJsonSchema and limit the claim to schema generation; do not assert it removes the runtime field or disables validation.

cases.title: Deprecation observables
cases.quote:
* a runtime deprecation warning emitted when accessing the field.
* `"deprecated": true` being set in the generated JSON schema.
cases.question: In Pydantic 2.10.6, what observable effects does marking a field deprecated have on field access and generated JSON schema?
cases.answer: Access emits a deprecation warning, and the generated schema contains deprecated: true.
cases.rubric: Require both effects; do not claim deprecation automatically deletes the field, forbids validation, or raises a validation error.

cases.title: Reuse an adapter in a loop
cases.start: ## Parsing data into a specified type
cases.quote:
it is recommended to create a `TypeAdapter` for a given type
    just once and reuse it in loops or other performance-critical code.
cases.question: In Pydantic 2.10.6, should performance-critical code recreate TypeAdapter for the same type on every loop iteration?
cases.answer: No. Construct it once for that type and reuse it, avoiding repeated type analysis and core-schema building.
cases.rubric: Require the reuse recommendation and construction overhead; do not invent a measured speedup or guarantee that all types share one adapter.

cases.title: Deferred schema construction
cases.quote:
If you set [`defer_build`][pydantic.config.ConfigDict.defer_build] to `True` when initializing a `TypeAdapter`,
Pydantic will defer building the core schema until the first time it is needed (for validation or serialization).
cases.question: In Pydantic 2.10.6, with TypeAdapter(..., config=ConfigDict(defer_build=True)), when is its schema built, and how can building be triggered explicitly?
cases.answer: It is deferred until first needed for validation or serialization; call the adapter's rebuild() method to trigger building explicitly.
cases.rubric: Require deferred first-use construction plus rebuild(); do not claim defer_build prevents validation permanently or makes unresolved references automatically valid.

cases.title: Adapter instances are not field types
cases.start:
!!! note
    Despite some overlap in use cases with
cases.end: ## Parsing data into a specified type
cases.quote:
[`TypeAdapter`][pydantic.type_adapter.TypeAdapter] should not be used as a type annotation for
    specifying fields of a `BaseModel`, etc.
cases.question: In Pydantic 2.10.6, should a TypeAdapter instance itself be used as the type annotation of a BaseModel field?
cases.answer: No. TypeAdapter is a validation/schema utility, not the field type annotation to use there.
cases.rubric: Require the annotation restriction; do not claim the underlying Pydantic-compatible type cannot be used in a field.

cases.title: After validator's input and return
cases.quote: - __*After* validators__: run after Pydantic's internal validation.
cases.question: In Pydantic 2.10.6, does a field after validator run before internal type validation, and may it omit returning the validated value?
cases.answer: No. It runs after internal validation and should return the validated value.
cases.rubric: Require both stage and value-return contract; do not conflate a field after validator with a model after validator returning the model instance.

cases.title: Before validator does not bypass type checks
cases.quote:
The value returned from this callable is then validated against the provided type annotation
  by Pydantic.
cases.question: In Pydantic 2.10.6, if a before field validator transforms raw input, does that transformation bypass Pydantic's subsequent validation against the field annotation?
cases.answer: No. Its returned value is still validated against the annotated field type.
cases.rubric: Require subsequent internal validation; distinguish before from plain validators, which can terminate validation.

cases.title: Plain validator short-circuit
cases.quote: so no further validators are called and Pydantic does not do any of its internal validation against the field type.
cases.question: In Pydantic 2.10.6, after a plain field validator returns, does Pydantic necessarily enforce the annotated field type through its usual internal validation?
cases.answer: No. A plain validator terminates validation, bypassing further validators and the usual internal field-type validation.
cases.rubric: Require the short-circuit behavior; do not generalize it to before or after validators.

cases.title: Wrap handler delegation
cases.quote:
You are free to wrap the call
    to the handler in a [`try..except`][handling exceptions] block, or not call it at all.
cases.question: In Pydantic 2.10.6, must a wrap field validator always invoke its handler, or may it return early and intercept validation errors?
cases.answer: It may intercept errors around handler delegation and may return early without calling the handler.
cases.rubric: Require optional delegation and control over validation flow; do not describe the handler as forbidden or automatically called despite an early return.

cases.title: Model after hooks return the instance
cases.quote:
Important note: the validated instance
  should be returned.
cases.question: In Pydantic 2.10.6, what should a model_validator(mode='after') return after checking an already validated model?
cases.answer: The validated model instance, normally self.
cases.rubric: Require returning the instance, not a field value or an arbitrary dictionary; distinguish this from a field validator's return contract.

cases.title: Before model inputs can be arbitrary
cases.quote: but they also have to deal with the raw input, which in theory could be any arbitrary object.
cases.question: In Pydantic 2.10.6, may a model_validator(mode='before') safely assume its raw input is always a dictionary?
cases.answer: No. The raw input can be an arbitrary object; check its shape before using dictionary-specific operations.
cases.rubric: Require that the input is not guaranteed to be a dict; do not claim dictionaries are never received or introduce an unrequested ORM configuration recipe.

cases.title: Order of Annotated validators
cases.quote: are run from right to left, and [*after*](#field-after-validator) validators are then run from left to right:
cases.question: In Pydantic 2.10.6, for validators in Annotated metadata, in which directions do before/wrap validators and then after validators run?
cases.answer: Before and wrap validators run right to left; after validators then run left to right.
cases.rubric: Require both directions and the phase ordering; do not reverse them or claim decorator order follows an unrelated rule.

cases.title: Inheritance and overridden validators
cases.quote: Overriding a model validator in a subclass will override the base class' validator, and thus only the subclass' version of said validator will be called.
cases.question: In Pydantic 2.10.6, if a subclass overrides an inherited model validator, are both the original and overriding versions automatically called?
cases.answer: No. Only the subclass's overriding version of that validator is called.
cases.rubric: Limit the answer to an actual override; do not claim every other distinct inherited validator is disabled or confuse it with model_config merging.

cases.title: Pass user context to validation
cases.quote:
You can pass a context object to the [validation methods](./models.md#validating-data), which can be accessed
inside the validator functions using the [`context`][pydantic.ValidationInfo.context] property:
cases.question: In Pydantic 2.10.6, how can a validator access a user-provided context object supplied to a validation method?
cases.answer: Pass context to the validation method and read it through ValidationInfo.context inside the validator.
cases.rubric: Require the method context argument and ValidationInfo.context access; do not invent global state or imply ordinary constructor calls automatically accept the same context argument.

cases.title: Unannotated arguments
cases.quote: Parameter types are inferred from type annotations on the function, or as [`Any`][typing.Any] if not annotated.
cases.question: In Pydantic 2.10.6, what type is assumed for a validate_call-decorated function parameter without a type annotation?
cases.answer: Any.
cases.rubric: Require Any; do not infer the type solely from its name or claim the parameter is rejected for lacking an annotation.

cases.title: Return values need opt-in validation
cases.quote:
By default, the return value of the function is **not** validated. To do so, the `validate_return` argument
    of the decorator can be set to `True`.
cases.question: In Pydantic 2.10.6, does validate_call validate a function's return value by default, and how is return validation enabled?
cases.answer: No. Set validate_return=True on the decorator to enable it.
cases.rubric: Require default-off plus the exact opt-in; do not confuse argument validation, which occurs before the call, with return validation.

cases.title: Async function support
cases.quote: [`validate_call()`][pydantic.validate_call] can also be used on async functions:
cases.question: In Pydantic 2.10.6, can validate_call decorate an async function, or is it restricted to synchronous functions?
cases.answer: It also supports async functions.
cases.rubric: Require async support; do not claim this turns an async function into a synchronous function or removes the need to await its coroutine.

cases.title: Nontrivial function signatures
cases.quote:
* Positional-only parameters: parameters before `, /`.
* Variable positional parameters defined via `*` (often `*args`).
* Variable keyword parameters defined via `**` (often `**kwargs`).
cases.question: In Pydantic 2.10.6, is validate_call limited to ordinary positional-or-keyword arguments, or does it also support positional-only, keyword-only, *args and **kwargs parameters?
cases.answer: It supports those parameter configurations and their combinations, including positional-only, keyword-only, *args, and **kwargs.
cases.rubric: Require support for the listed shapes without changing Python's own calling rules; do not claim arbitrary positional passing becomes valid for keyword-only parameters.
